questions.stem: Find the synonym of the word: 'METICULOUS'
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. 'Fastidious' is a close synonym, meaning very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail. 
DECOY BUSTING: 'Sloppy' and 'Hasty' are antonyms (meaning careless or rushed). 'Apathetic' means showing no interest or emotion.
EXAM INSIGHT: Use it in a sentence: 'The accountant was meticulous in his record-keeping, never missing a single receipt.' Other synonyms include scrupulous, punctilious, and painstaking.

questions.stem: Find the synonym of the word: 'EPHEMERAL'
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time. 'Transient' similarly means lasting only for a short time; impermanent.
DECOY BUSTING: 'Eternal' is the exact antonym (lasting forever). 'Substantial' means having solid worth or mass. 'Luminous' means emitting light.
EXAM INSIGHT: Think of an ephemeral stream (one that only flows briefly after rain) or the ephemeral beauty of a sunset. Synonyms: fleeting, passing, short-lived, momentary.

questions.stem: Find the synonym of the word: 'OBFUSCATE'
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'Obfuscate' means to render obscure, unclear, or unintelligible. Politicians often 'obfuscate' the truth by giving long, complicated answers that confuse the public. 'Confuse' is the direct synonym.
DECOY BUSTING: 'Clarify' and 'Illuminate' are antonyms (meaning to make clear). 'Rectify' means to put right or correct a mistake.
EXAM INSIGHT: Obfuscate comes from the Latin root 'obfuscare' (to darken). It is a high-frequency GRE/Bank PO word used when someone intentionally makes a situation murky or complicated to avoid giving a straight answer.

questions.stem: Find the synonym of the word: 'GREGARIOUS'
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'Gregarious' describes a person who is fond of company; outgoing and friendly. 'Sociable' is the exact synonym. 
DECOY BUSTING: 'Introverted' is the antonym (shy, preferring to be alone). 'Hostile' means aggressive. 'Melancholy' means sad or depressed.
EXAM INSIGHT: It comes from the Latin 'grex', meaning 'flock'. A gregarious animal (like a sheep) lives in flocks. A gregarious human loves to be surrounded by the 'flock' at parties.
